# In the Kumārasambhava

### Verse 28
"May you receive the undivided love of your husband," thus Umā was addressed by those women as she bowed. By her, however, who was to share half of his body, even the blessings of her dear ones were surpassed.

**Commentary:**
Regarding "undivided": The bowing and prostrating Umā was addressed by those virtuous women, who said, "May you attain the unbroken, perfect love of your husband, Shiva." The phrase "was addressed" <note>Sanskrit: ucyate sma</note> uses the present tense with the particle "sma" to indicate the past tense. Because she shared half of the body of Hara <gloss>Shiva</gloss>—forming the compound "half-body-sharer" <note>Sanskrit: ardhaśarīrabhājā</note>—the blessings of her relatives and dear ones were surpassed or rendered secondary. The inner meaning is that she obtained a result even greater than their blessings, as she became physically one with him.

### Verse 29
The skillful Mountain, having completed every necessary task for her according to his desires and wealth, stood as a fit member in the assembly hall filled with friends, awaiting the arrival of the Bull-bannered God.

**Commentary:**
Regarding "desire": The skillful and capable <note>Sanskrit: kṛtī</note> Mountain, Himavān, completed <gloss>leaving no remainder</gloss> the duties and rites for Pārvatī in a manner suited to his intent and his majesty. The word "fit member" <note>Sanskrit: sabhyaḥ</note> refers to one who is worthy of an assembly. He remained in the gathering <gloss>saṃsad</gloss> which was occupied by his kinsmen. He is described as "awaiting the arrival of the Bull-bannered" <note>Sanskrit: vṛṣāṅkāgamana-pratīkṣaḥ</note>, meaning he was waiting for the arrival of Hara <gloss>Shiva</gloss>.

### Verse 30
Meanwhile, on the mountain of Kubera, the finery suitable for that impending marriage was placed before Bhava, the destroyer of the cities, by the Mothers who had been respectfully summoned.

**Commentary:**
Regarding "meanwhile": This refers to the same time that Pārvatī’s preparation was occurring. On the mountain of Kubera <gloss>Mount Kailāsa</gloss>, the materials for decoration and finery <gloss>prasādhana</gloss> suitable for the marriage were brought. These were presented by the Mothers <gloss>the Seven Mothers beginning with Brāhmī</gloss> who had been summoned with great respect. These items were placed before the "Destroyer of the Cities" <note>Sanskrit: puraśāsana</note>, an epithet for Bhava <gloss>Shiva</gloss>.

<summary>Pārvatī receives blessings of total union with Shiva while her father Himavān prepares the wedding assembly. Simultaneously, the Seven Mothers prepare the wedding finery for Shiva on Mount Kailāsa.</summary>
